Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: Can MVFA's segmentation adapters learn transferable localisation from image-level labels alone? Today they learn only from pixel masks of BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC. We replace the Dice and Focal seg_loss with a multiple-instance objective applied at all four levels to the segmentation-branch patch-to-text similarity map (mean of the top 2% patch anomaly probabilities; max and mean pooling as ablations), and train on all five source datasets with masks discarded. Primary question and hypothesis: because every patch is scored against a shared text anchor, image-level supervision aligns patch-level evidence with the text 'abnormal' direction, so the learned localisation transfers to the unseen modality and retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-level AUROC (with PRO and image AUROC also reported). A visual-only MIL control (same operator on a linear patch classifier without text anchors) tests whether text anchoring is responsible. Secondary analyses: per-level localisation quality, and a label-budget comparison on two held-out modalities between image-labelled training and mask-supervised training on 10%, 30% and 100% of the masked images.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Optimal-transport label assignment of abnormal mass to patches under a lesion-fraction budget
SUMMARY: Assign the 'abnormal' label of each abnormal training image to its patches by entropic optimal transport, with a mass budget equal to the dataset's estimated lesion fraction and costs from the current segmentation scores, as modern object detectors assign labels to anchors.
HYPOTHESIS: OT-based dynamic label assignment retains at least 85% of mask-supervised MVFA's held-out pixel-AUROC margin over chance and improves PRO by at least 1.5 points over PU learning with the same lesion-fraction estimate.
RATIONALE: By analogy with optimal-transport label assignment in object detection (OTA), where ground-truth objects distribute their labels over many candidate anchors by solving a transport problem rather than by fixed rules, an abnormal image's label can be distributed over its patches: a fixed amount of 'abnormal mass' (the expected lesion fraction) flows preferentially to patches that the model currently scores as abnormal and that are spatially contiguous. Unlike PU's exchangeable treatment, this produces sharp, per-image soft labels that adapt during training.
METHOD: 1) Lesion fraction pi_d per dataset by mixture proportion estimation (as for PU). 2) Per abnormal image, OT between supplies {abnormal: pi_d * N, normal: (1 - pi_d) * N} and the N patches with cost c_j(abnormal) = -log p_j + lambda_s * (1 - neighbourhood mean of p), c_j(normal) = -log(1 - p_j); Sinkhorn with epsilon 0.1, 50 iterations, no gradient. 3) Soft labels = transport plan rows; BCE on patches with these labels; normal images all-normal. 4) Warm-up 5 epochs with asymmetric MIL. 5) Code: loss.py ota_assign(); train_zero.py.
EXPERIMENT: BMAD zero-shot leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); no source masks used by the proposed variants; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as reference; 3 seeds; pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Baselines: PU learning; asymmetric MIL; mask-supervised MVFA. Ablations: lambda_s; epsilon; budget misspecification. Metrics: held-out pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC. Falsification: no PRO gain over PU.

Idea B:
TITLE: Bank-informed positive-unlabelled learning: patch-specific class priors from position-aware normal-bank distances
SUMMARY: Train MVFA's segmentation adapters with non-negative PU learning, but replace the single dataset-level class prior with patch-specific priors derived from position-aware normal-bank distances, so likely-lesion patches carry more of the unlabelled positive mass.
HYPOTHESIS: Patch-specific priors improve held-out pixel AUROC by at least 1 point and PRO by at least 2 points over PU learning with a single dataset-level prior, and the combined method retains at least 85% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-AUROC margin over chance.
RATIONALE: Parent 1 (PU learning) uses every patch of abnormal images but treats them as exchangeable, with one class prior per dataset, which reviewers flagged as fragile for small lesions; parent 2 (position-aware bank) provides a per-patch, anatomy-aware estimate of how unusual each patch is. Weighted PU risk estimators accept instance-dependent priors, so the bank's evidence can be injected in a principled way, keeping a single training objective.
METHOD: 1) Position-aware bank distances d_j per abnormal-image patch (radius 2, 20% coreset per position). 2) Patch prior pi_j = pi_d * softmax_j(d_j / T) * N_patches, clipped to [0, 0.9], where pi_d is the dataset-level prior from mixture proportion estimation and T is chosen so the mean prior equals pi_d. 3) Weighted nnPU loss with instance priors (negatives labelled: normal-image patches). 4) Balanced batches (4 normal + 4 abnormal, same dataset); lr 1e-4, 50 epochs. 5) Code: estimate_prior.py, make_banks.py, loss.py weighted_nnpu().
EXPERIMENT: BMAD zero-shot leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); no source masks used by the proposed variants; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as reference; 3 seeds; pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Baselines: PU with a single prior; position-aware bank pseudo-masks; asymmetric MIL; mask-supervised MVFA. Ablations: temperature T; radius. Metrics: held-out pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC. Falsification: no gain over single-prior PU.

CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
